      <title>Diego Gómez hits another stunner as Brighton beat 10-man Brentford to go second</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/08/brighton-brentford-premier-league-match-report</link>
      <description><p></p><p>Who can stop Brighton’s ­ascension in English and European football? They are setting standards, ­practices ­leaving almost everybody else ­trailing in their wake. A ­second‑place position in the ­Premier&nbsp;League would once have read like a glitch in a ­Football ­Manager ­session. Not in November 2026, where they appear the only team capable of throwing down any sort of challenge to Arsenal.</p><p>Under low winter sun, Brentford, an opposition to which Brighton are often, if lazily, compared, were ­swatted aside. If Keith Andrews’s team, and their fans at the Amex&nbsp;­Stadium, could level blame at a couple of ­refereeing decisions, they received little chance of rescuing anything. Brighton squeezed them, toyed with them.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/08/brighton-brentford-premier-league-match-report">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <description><p>A lot can change in five‑and‑a‑half months, but as an early winter chill descended on Wearside last week – both meteorologically and metaphorically – Sunderland were determined that some things should remain the same.       <description><p>It was the moment when Liverpool knew they would win here in south London and so move on from the Premier League loss to Arsenal at Anfield last Sunday and the one in midweek at Fenerbahce in the Champions League.</p><p>Florian Wirtz had timed his run as Liverpool broke up the right and Bradley Barcola’s low pull back was made to measure. Wirtz had to take it on first time and it was a test of his technique under pressure. He never looked like failing it, not least because smoothness in this area is his calling card. Liverpool were 2-0 up, Alexis Mac Allister having headed them in front towards the end of the first half, and all you could hear was the eruption of delight in the away supporters’ enclosure.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/08/crystal-palace-liverpool-premier-league-match-report">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Enzo Maresca rues Manchester City’s lack of desire after defeat at Nottingham Forest</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/07/enzo-maresca-nottingham-forest-manchester-city-premier-league</link>
      <description><ul><li><p>‘You need desire and intensity … we didn’t match them’</p></li><li><p>City have now lost three successive league matches</p></li></ul><p>Enzo Maresca blamed his side’s lack of desire and the way they were outgunned in duels for a third successive Premier League defeat. After winning their first seven games of the season, <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/07/nottingham-forest-manchester-city-premier-league-match-report">Manchester City’s 3-1 loss at Nottingham Forest</a> extended their poor run.</p><p>Jair Cunha dispossessed Josko Gvardiol to score the opener, then Liam Delap struck twice with muscular surges on the break as Forest won their first home league game since April. “Today I think [the problem] has been general,” said Maresca. “It’s not about one player. In the first half we lost all the duels, all the contacts. Against this team, that is fighting relegation, if you don’t match them … it’s something we need to understand. In this kind of game, if you’re not able to win duels and second balls like in the first half, you struggle.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/07/enzo-maresca-nottingham-forest-manchester-city-premier-league">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <title>Thierno Barry double fires Everton to comeback win against Coventry</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/06/everton-coventry-premier-league-match-report</link>
      <description><p>The wildly optimistic Evertonian – if such a being exists – could not have envisaged David Moyes’ side <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/premierleague/table">fifth in the Premier League</a> with Thierno Barry just behind Erling Haaland in the goalscoring chart when their transfer window closed in calamitous fashion. Yet there they sit, team and striker defying all expectations, following a stirring comeback against luckless Coventry.</p><p>Frank Lampard endured a torturous night against his old club as Coventry impressed but were refused two&nbsp;strong penalty claims. The Coventry manager felt his team were denied a third time by the video assistant referee for an apparent handball by Barry when edging Everton ahead. Replays were inconclusive. It was the dancing French forward’s second goal of the game and 10th in all competitions this season. He also delivered a fine assist for Kiernan Dewsbury-Hall as the in-form midfielder put his latest England disappointment behind him to seal victory in convincing style.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/06/everton-coventry-premier-league-match-report">Continue reading...</a></description>

      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/06/premier-league-10-things-to-look-out-for-this-weekend</link>
      <description><p>Lampard appreciation at Everton, Glasner sparking Forest fire, Zubimendi and Kroupi in spotlight and Carrick v Emery</p><ul><li><p><a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/sep/10/premier-league-top-scorers-2026-27-race-for-golden-boot">Premier League top scorers</a></p></li></ul><p>Nothing better encapsulates the dysfunction that was Everton under Farhad Moshiri than the idea that an unknown vandal with a can of spray paint could influence the club’s managerial direction. “Pereira out, Lampard in” they daubed on a wall at Goodison Park when it appeared Vítor Pereira was in line to replace Rafael Benítez in 2022. Alarmed by fan protests, the Everton board opted instead for Frank Lampard and, while his tenure ended 12 months later with the club immersed in another relegation battle, there will be appreciation for the Coventry manager when he makes a first visit to Hill Dickinson Stadium on Friday. The connection between Lampard and Evertonians was genuine and a factor in keeping the club up in 2022. Both parties will be glad to see the other emerging stronger from those troubled times.       <title>The international break is almost here: so wave goodbye to your players, and maybe your manager | Max Rushden</title>
      <link>https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/05/the-international-break-is-almost-here-so-wave-goodbye-to-your-players-and-maybe-your-manager</link>
      <description><p>What used to be a time to reset is now a time to rehire, and Michael Carrick is not the only Premier League manager looking over his shoulder</p><p>Perhaps the most telling moment of Manchester United’s <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/03/manchester-united-roma-champions-league-match-report">comeback against Roma</a> was at the final whistle. The camera focused on Michael Carrick, who shook the hand of Gian Piero Gasperini before looking around trying to remember what you’re meant to do after a victory. The camera then cut to the director of football, Jason Wilcox, and chief executive, Omar Berrada, clapping with two of the most ashen faces you could imagine – as if it was a minute’s applause in the 87th minute for a lifelong, octogenarian fan who died peacefully in his sleep earlier in the week (most probably not at a United game but you couldn’t rule it out).</p><p>Of course, there are rules about smiling when you are involved with a failing football club. Players can’t be seen to be enjoying themselves in the week after a defeat, managers have to be earnest at almost all times, apart from when a journalist’s phone goes off at a press conference – a moment of sporting hilarity on a par with a pigeon landing on Centre Court.</p> <a href="https://www.theguardian.com/football/2026/nov/05/the-international-break-is-almost-here-so-wave-goodbye-to-your-players-and-maybe-your-manager">Continue reading...</a></description>
